subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should ordinary `message(action="send")` hide poll creation fields from the model-facing schema, strip accidental poll fields at runtime, or keep rejecting content-bearing poll fields as explicit poll intent?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses the shared message-tool schema, outbound validation, and channel delivery contract; choosing schema scoping versus runtime sanitization is a product/API decision automation should not settle from this issue alone.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for `poll` or channel-specific poll surfaces so plain sends cannot inherit them while strict poll validation remains intact.

options.title: Sanitize send params
options.body: Treat `action="send"` as authoritative and strip poll creation fields before delivery, improving send reliability while silently discarding poll-looking content on send.

options.title: Keep strict guard
options.body: Preserve the shipped content-bearing rejection and close only if maintainers decide the metadata/default fixes are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for `poll` or channel-specific poll surfaces so plain sends cannot inherit them while strict poll validation remains intact.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged poll gating and message-tool schema consistency work is the strongest feature-history signal for the shared send/poll contract boundary.
